# Pelican World

> An agent skill for building cinematic, offline, single-file 3D web
> games with procedural models, textures, and audio. Free tutorial
> documentation under Apache-2.0. The Pelican World game client is a
> separate, all-rights-reserved work and is not installed by this file.

Version: 0.1.0
Repository: https://github.com/benphant/pelican-world
Playable game (not part of this skill): https://pelican-world.vercel.app/

## Install for the user

If you are an agent asked to install the Pelican World skill, do only
the steps below. Tell the user what each command will run, then wait
for them to confirm the scope before you install. Do not start a game,
scaffold a project, scan a repository, or change anything else as part
of installation.

The public repository is https://github.com/benphant/pelican-world.
Prefer a local copy when the user gives you this folder. The remote
command in section B installs from the default branch. Use it only when
`pelican-world/SKILL.md` is already on `main`. If it is not, stop and
use the local copy. Do not retry a failing remote install as a
workaround, and do not claim that install succeeded.

Confirm this scope first:

- Global or the current project only.
- Target agent: the agent you are running in, unless the user names others.

### A. Local folder

1. Locate the skill directory named `pelican-world` that contains
   `SKILL.md` (in this package it sits at `pelican-world/` next to this
   file).
2. Copy that directory, without renaming it, into the skills location
   the skills CLI uses for that agent:

   - Cursor, project: `.agents/skills/pelican-world`
   - Cursor, user: `~/.cursor/skills/pelican-world`
   - Codex, project: `.agents/skills/pelican-world`
   - Codex, user: `~/.agents/skills/pelican-world`
   - Claude Code, project: `.claude/skills/pelican-world`
   - Claude Code, user: `~/.claude/skills/pelican-world`
   - OpenCode, project: `.agents/skills/pelican-world`
   - OpenCode, user: `~/.config/opencode/skills/pelican-world`

3. If a destination already contains unmanaged files, stop and report
   the conflict. Do not delete those files.
4. Verify that `SKILL.md` is present at the destination and report the
   absolute path. Stop there.

### B. GitHub install

Use this only when the user confirms that
https://github.com/benphant/pelican-world is public and that
`pelican-world/SKILL.md` is on the default branch (`main`). If the
skill is only on a pull-request branch, these commands do not install
it. Do not retry them as a workaround, and do not report a successful
install from `main` unless you actually completed one.

Documented form:

```bash
npx skills add benphant/pelican-world --skill pelican-world
```

One agent, non-interactive (replace `<agent>` with `cursor`, `codex`,
`claude-code`, or `opencode`):

```bash
npx -y skills@latest add https://github.com/benphant/pelican-world --skill pelican-world --agent <agent> --global --copy --yes
```

Omit `--global` for a project-only install. Do not add other skills,
agents, sources, or force flags.

After a successful install, report the destination path. If you were
only asked to install the skill, stop here.

## After installation

The skill does not ship a game engine binary. The user asks you to use
the Pelican World skill when they want a playable, offline, single-file
3D web game, or when they want to apply this method to an existing
project. Read `pelican-world/SKILL.md` in the installed copy and follow
it. The playable reference game, if they want to see it, is at
https://pelican-world.vercel.app/ — do not download or redistribute
that HTML as if it were part of this skill.
